title: If Anything, You Should Be Slowing Things Down
author: The Daily Dad
summary: This Daily Dad entry targets the reflexive habit of hurrying children through errands, school drop-offs and everyday routines. It points out the irony that rushing rarely buys anything: it only leads to the next activity or the next request for screen time, while spending down the limited years of childhood. The reflection offers ordinary scenes, a Saturday grocery run or watching a child chat with friends outside school, and asks why parents are trying to get them over with. Its central reframing is that parenting has no finish line worth reaching, since the end point is the moment children no longer need a parent to drive them or wait for them. The piece closes with a plain instruction to stop, or at least slow down, and to notice children growing up. It ends with a product plug for a Tempus Fugit medallion.
points: The piece argues that hurrying children rarely gains anything except a faster route to the next activity or screen-time negotiation.
Ordinary moments like a weekend grocery trip or a school pickup are recast as the time with children a parent will later miss.
Its key reversal is that the finish line parents rush toward is the very thing they should be trying to avoid.
The advice applies across ages, from a two-year-old to a twenty-year-old, because the window is always closing.
quotes: We are always rushing our kids, rushing through things—as if it’s not clear where all this is heading.
Right now, we have them. We are at the grocery store on a Saturday. That’s wonderful! Why are we trying to finish that quickly?
Right now, we have them, whether they are a 2-year-old, a 12-year-old, or a 20-year-old. Why are we trying to get this over with?
This is life. Not only is there not a finish line—the finish line is the thing we are desperately trying to avoid.
At some point, they won’t need us to drive them. To wait for them. They won’t need us any longer. They will be adults.
This is what we’re going to miss. Yet here we are, rushing through it, rushing them.
